name: Aperture Finance arbitrary call approval drain

classification.summary: The closed-source Aperture router forwarded caller-supplied call targets and calldata without validation, letting the attacker make the contract invoke ERC-20 transferFrom() and ERC-721 transfers against the standing token and Uniswap V3 position approvals users had granted it.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

limitations: Target identity and code history came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/aperture-finance.json; no semantic revalidation was inherited.
The executing code artifact and its code hash have not been established in structured evidence.
One or more target block, transaction, ordering, or creator anchors remain unresolved.

sources.note: onchain review: victim created 2025-12-15 by 0xbeef63ae5a2102506e8a352a5bb32aa8b30b3112 (not the attacker), no EIP-1967 Upgraded event before the incident. The anchored tx is the attacker's contract-creation tx; its logs show 36.918 WBTC pulled from user 0x5240b03be5bc101a0082074666dd89ad883e1f9d to the attacker EOA plus a Uniswap V3 position mint. Reported incident total $3.67M across Ethereum/Arbitrum/Base.

limitations: Classification and loss came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/aperture-finance.json; legacy measurement.status=OK is provenance only.
